You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To crush peanuts, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase raw peanuts from the market (45 minutes)
Step 2. Clean the work surface thoroughly (10 minutes)
Step 3. Sort through peanuts to remove debris (20 minutes)
Step 4. Rinse the peanuts under cold water (5 minutes)
Step 5. Transfer peanuts to the crushing vessel (2 minutes)
Step 6. Inspect the texture of the crushed nuts (30 seconds)
Step 7. Clear a space on the kitchen counter (5 minutes)
Step 8. Gather all necessary bowls (5 minutes)
Step 9. Measure the quantity of peanuts needed (3 minutes)
Step 10. Dry the peanuts with a clean towel (10 minutes)
Step 11. Store the crushed peanuts in a jar (4 minutes)
Step 12. Preheat the oven for light roasting (15 minutes)
Step 13. Clean the crushing tool (5 minutes)
Step 14. Wash your hands (1 minute)
Step 15. Shell the peanuts (1 hour)
Step 16. Spread peanuts on a baking sheet (3 minutes)
Step 17. Locate the heavy-duty mortar and pestle (5 minutes)
Step 18. Remove the red papery skins (30 minutes)
Step 19. Set the timer for the cooling process (1 minute)
Step 20. Sanitize the nut cracker (5 minutes)
Step 21. Begin the manual crushing motion (10 minutes)
Step 22. Adjust the grip on the pestle (30 seconds)
Step 23. Check the stability of the table (2 minutes)
Step 24. Place a cloth under the mortar to prevent slipping (1 minute)
Step 25. Check the humidity in the room (1 minute)
Step 26. Wipe down the interior of the bowl (2 minutes)
Step 27. Sharpen the edge of a chopping knife (8 minutes)
Step 28. Dice any unusually large peanut halves (12 minutes)
Step 29. Check the expiration date on the package (1 minute)
Step 30. Organize the workspace for efficiency (10 minutes)
Step 31. Sift out the fine peanut dust (5 minutes)
Step 32. Prepare a secondary collection bowl (2 minutes)
Step 33. Retrieve a stool to sit on (2 minutes)
Step 34. Label the storage container (3 minutes)
Step 35. Calibrate the kitchen scale (4 minutes)
Step 36. Put on a kitchen apron (1 minute)
Step 37. Spread the nuts out to reach room temperature (20 minutes)
Step 38. Plug in the overhead light (1 minute)
Step 39. Select the desired coarseness level (2 minutes)
Step 40. Put on safety glasses (1 minute)
Step 41. Tie back long hair (1 minute)
Step 42. Verify the oven temperature with a thermometer (5 minutes)
Step 43. Prepare a damp cloth for spills (2 minutes)
Step 44. Check the sturdiness of the floor (1 minute)
Step 45. Clear the sink of any dishes (15 minutes)
Step 46. Sweep the floor of the prep area (10 minutes)
Step 47. Roast peanuts lightly for better flavor (12 minutes)
Step 48. Open the window for ventilation (1 minute)
Step 49. Double-check the recipe requirements (5 minutes)
Step 50. Pour the peanuts into a cooling tray (2 minutes)
Step 51. Shake the peanuts in a mesh bag (5 minutes)
Step 52. Arrange the tools in order of use (5 minutes)
Step 53. Discard the empty shells and skins (5 minutes)
Step 54. Let the peanuts cool completely (40 minutes)
Step 55. Sift out any remaining small stones (6 minutes)
Step 56. Final quality check of the batch (3 minutes)
Step 57. Check for any allergic warnings (2 minutes)
Step 58. Find the bag of peanuts in the pantry (2 minutes)
Step 59. Set aside a small portion for garnishing (3 minutes)
Step 60. Position the mortar in the center of the tray (1 minute)
Step 61. Sharpen the manual hand-crank blades (10 minutes)
Step 62. Tighten the screws on the nut grinder (3 minutes)
Step 63. Wash the roasting pan (10 minutes)
Step 64. Place a lid over the finished product (30 seconds)
Step 65. Turn on the kitchen fan (30 seconds)
Step 66. Wash the measuring cups (5 minutes)
Step 67. Close the pantry door (30 seconds)
Step 68. Dry the interior of the storage jar (2 minutes)
Step 69. Clean the counter of any shell fragments (8 minutes)
Step 70. Remove jewelry from hands (2 minutes)
Step 71. Put on latex-free gloves (2 minutes)
Step 72. Seal the waste bag (1 minute)
Step 73. Pour a glass of water for the worker (1 minute)
Step 74. Wipe the outside of the mortar (3 minutes)
Step 75. Collect the skins for composting (4 minutes)
Step 76. Check the lighting in the kitchen (2 minutes)
Step 77. Rinse the chopping board (4 minutes)
Step 78. Clear the dining table (15 minutes)
Step 79. Vacuum any dust from the floor (10 minutes)
Step 80. Secure the grinder to the tabletop (5 minutes)
Step 81. Pre-heat the storage jar to prevent moisture (10 minutes)
Step 82. Read the instructions for the grinder (5 minutes)
Step 83. Brush the fine particles into the bowl (3 minutes)
Step 84. Weigh the raw peanuts (4 minutes)
Step 85. Clean the kitchen scale (5 minutes)
Step 86. Break the peanuts into smaller chunks by hand (15 minutes)
Step 87. Pat the peanuts dry after rinsing (5 minutes)
Step 88. Shake the peanuts to remove loose debris (2 minutes)
Step 89. Place the pestle next to the mortar (1 minute)
Step 90. Take off the kitchen apron (1 minute)
